description: all over a class population follows newly created instances
code:
class Light(on):
    this.on = on
hall = Light(true)
desk = Light(true)
allOn = all light in Light: light.on
assert(allOn, true)
porch = Light(false)
assert(allOn, false)
porch.on = true
allOn

description: any over a list of due dates follows the list and today
code:
today = 30
dues = [10, 45, 60]
overdue = any due in dues: due < today
assert(overdue, true)
dues = [45, 60]
assert(overdue, false)
today = 50
overdue

description: Nested quantifiers check that every course has a matching teacher
code:
class Course(topic):
    this.topic = topic
class Teacher(topic):
    this.topic = topic
Course("math")
Course("art")
Teacher("math")
staffed = all c in Course: any t in Teacher: t.topic == c.topic
assert(staffed, false)
Teacher("art")
staffed

description: A class-level rule quantifies over each cart's own items
code:
class Item(price):
    this.price = price
class Cart(items):
    this.items = items
$Cart.affordable = all item in $Cart.items: item.price <= 20
cheap = Item(5)
pricey = Item(50)
basket = Cart([cheap, pricey])
assert(basket.affordable, false)
pricey.price = 15
basket.affordable

description: all over a why selection checks every value behind a total
code:
base = 4
rate = base * 2
total = rate + 1
positive = all step in why total: step.holds > 0
assert(positive, true)
base = -4
positive

description: A function body quantifies over its parameter
code:
def allEven(values) => all v in values: v % 2 == 0
numbers = [2, 4]
even = allEven(numbers)
assert(even, true)
numbers.push(3)
even

description: Variables named all and any stay ordinary beside quantifiers
code:
all = [3, 6, 9]
any = 2
big = all n in all: n > any
assert(big, true)
any = 5
big
